name: Export bill entries stay open after payment arrives
plain: Indian banks track each export bill until payment is matched to it, and entries stay open when the payment is not mapped, is a few dollars short or went to another bank. Example: a $1,000 bill paid $980 stays open until the exporter writes a letter.
frequency_reason: Banks close bills monthly (L6#19); every short or unmapped receipt.
severity_reason: Rs 12,000 penalty (L6#19), up to Rs 1,400 per bill (L6#20), entries open for years (L4#8).
unsolved_reason: The Rs 10 lakh declaration helps but is discretionary (L4#10, L6#25); no tool maps receipts to bills.
solvable_reason: An agent maps each Airwallex deposit to its invoice and shipping bill, sends the bank the right reference and drafts the 'close as bank charges' letter; the bank must act.
build_call_reason: Survives with long-running evidence, no tool does it, and an agent can map deposits to bills and draft closure letters.
workaround_today: Exporter-built Excel IRM (L6#19); request letters to the bank (L6#23); ask each bank for its own pending list (L6#22).
code_decides: Map deposit to bill and compute shortfall

name: SWIFT middle banks take fees so receipts arrive short
plain: When a customer abroad sends a wire, banks along the way quietly take a fee, so less arrives than the invoice says. Example: a $1,000 invoice lands as $984 and the seller must work out why.
segments: G1 G2 G3 G4 G7 GX
frequency_reason: Repeats on every SWIFT receipt on affected routes: 'frequently' (L1#31), USD 16 'each time' (L7#29).
severity_reason: Each gap is small (FSB 0.1-1.3%, L5#28; about USD 20, L1#32) but in India it keeps export bills open (L2#33).
unsolved_reason: Booking is solved by a fee line, but no tool explains the cause and the sent amount is unknown (L2#31: ask the customer).
solvable_reason: An agent can explain the gap and move USD payers onto local ACH details on a Global Account, removing the SWIFT leg; OUR is still not guaranteed (L5#10).
build_call_reason: Survives the skeptic, recurs on every USD SWIFT receipt, and the cause fix (local rails on a Global Account) is native to Airwallex.
workaround_today: Book a negative bank-charge line; ask the customer how much they sent; tell payers to choose OUR.
ai_reads: Deposit amount, payer bank and route
code_decides: Compare gap to known fee bands and route
person_approves: Writing off the fee or switching the payer to local rails

name: Invoice currency differs from the currency received
plain: The invoice is in one currency but money arrives in another, so amounts never match and someone posts the difference by hand. Example: a USD invoice is paid in EUR or lands converted into GBP.
frequency_reason: The deposit 'always differs' (L1#35); 2026 comments on the 55-vote idea (L2#16).
severity_reason: A manual clearing journal every time; Zoho turns it into unusable credit (L2#27).
unsolved_reason: A clearing-account workaround exists everywhere, but no native fix.
solvable_reason: Receiving into a same-currency Global Account removes conversion at receipt; the agent decides keep or convert with FX quotes.
build_call_reason: Survives and Airwallex removes the cause, but for Airwallex users invoicing in the receipt currency it mostly disappears; it belongs to the keep-or-convert feature.
workaround_today: Clearing account plus a manual FX journal (L2#16).
code_decides: Keep or convert using a locked FX quote

name: Customers' bank-change checks slow switching to new details
plain: When a seller asks a customer to pay into new bank details, the customer's accounts team must verify it by phone, forms and approvals, often freezing payments meanwhile. Example: a callback then a two-week wait before the new account is used.
frequency_reason: Once per customer switch, not weekly; but every corporate payer runs the check (L8#26, L8#35).
severity_reason: Two-week freeze (L8#1), 48-hour letterhead step and activation on the next invoice (L8#20), 5+ days international (L8#19).
unsolved_reason: No tool prepares the seller's side; payer controls are tightening (Nacha 2026, L8#26).
solvable_reason: An agent can assemble what payers ask for (letter with old and new details, last three remittances from Airwallex deposits, L8#22, L8#23) and confirm the switch on the first deposit.
build_call_reason: The core fix depends on it; it survives the skeptic, no tool prepares the seller's side, and Airwallex data supplies the proof payers ask for.
workaround_today: Phone callbacks, signed letterhead PDFs, portal updates by the seller.
code_decides: Fill old and new details and last remittances

name: Matching picks the wrong invoice or customer
plain: Tools match on amount or a shared word, so a payment lands on the wrong, similarly named customer or a cancelled invoice. Example: two customers both called 'Acme' and a $500 payment goes to the wrong one.
frequency_reason: 'Keeps matching to the wrong customer' (L2#10); amount-first matching is the default (L1#22).
severity_reason: Wrong ledgers lead to wrong chasing and cleanup.
unsolved_reason: Seen in Xero, ERPNext and Invoice Ninja in 2025-2026 (L2#10, L7#7, L7#37).
solvable_reason: A dedicated Global Account per customer gives unambiguous attribution; the agent checks reference, payer and amount together (L6#10).
build_call_reason: Survives, unsolved in current tools, and a per-customer Global Account removes the ambiguity at the source.
workaround_today: Check every auto-match by hand.
code_decides: Require account, reference and amount to agree

name: Bank feed cuts the reference and leaves the payer blank
plain: The bank feed into accounting software chops the payment reference or puts the payer in the wrong field, so matching falls back to amount. Example: 'INV-1043 ACME' arrives as 'INV-10'.
frequency_reason: Every transaction on affected feeds is typed by hand (L1#27); threads July-October 2026.
severity_reason: Wrong matches on amount alone (L2#13); bank rules do not scale past 70 accounts (L1#26).
unsolved_reason: Xero says the bank controls the field (L1#25); marked 'Gaining Support' in October 2026.
solvable_reason: The agent reads payer and reference from the Airwallex Deposits API, bypassing the feed; the reference is still one free-text string (L5#0).
build_call_reason: Survives with current threads, Xero says it cannot fix it, and reading Airwallex deposits directly removes the feed from the path.
workaround_today: Type the contact by hand; one bank rule per customer.
ai_reads: Deposit payer and reference from the API
code_decides: Match on full reference and account

name: Incoming payments held for review or bounced
plain: The receiving provider puts a customer's payment under review, sometimes sending it back, so the seller is not paid. Example: a client's invoice payment is flagged and returned, and the seller refunds the client from their own pocket.
frequency_reason: Rare: 13 of 171 Airwallex reviews (7.6%) describe an incoming-payment hold, only 2 on a first payment or new account (F3 follow-up); docs say most deposits auto-clear (L3#20).
severity_reason: Payments bounced, seller repaid customers itself (L3#1), USD 5,000 lost (L3#30).
unsolved_reason: No tool helps; no provider publishes a hold rate.
solvable_reason: An agent can answer DEPOSIT-linked RFIs fast with the invoice or contract (L5#6, L5#7); the hold decision stays with Airwallex.
build_call_reason: Real but rare: the follow-up confirmed 13 of 171 Airwallex Trustpilot reviews as incoming-payment holds, mostly later or large payments, and the hold decision is Airwallex's. Handle held deposits and document requests (PENDING and RFI webhooks) in the build, but don't lead with it. (Changed from build_first after the 21 Oct follow-up.)
workaround_today: Upload verification documents again and again (L3#30); contact support.
code_decides: Attach the matching invoice and contract

name: Incomplete wire instructions cause extra conversions and cuts
plain: If the seller's payment instructions leave out the middle bank or a 'do not convert' note, the payer's bank picks a route that converts the money or takes extra cuts. Example: USD sent to a USD account is turned into EUR and back.
frequency_reason: unknown: shared as a practitioner tip with no rate given (L1#2, L8#13).
severity_reason: Needless double conversion and deductions plus delays (L5#19); amounts not stated.
unsolved_reason: Nothing generates correct per-currency instructions; sellers rely on forum tips (L8#12).
solvable_reason: Airwallex publishes intermediary and correspondent tables per Global Account (L5#19); an agent can issue exact instructions for the right currency account.
build_call_reason: A cheap cause fix but thinly evidenced (4 items); ship it inside the short-payment fix rather than alone.
workaround_today: Add 'DO NOT CONVERT' and name the intermediary bank on wire instructions.
ai_reads: Payer's bank country and past deposit routes
code_decides: Pick the Global Account and intermediary to quote
person_approves: Sending new instructions to the customer

name: Payer name on the deposit differs from the customer
plain: The money shows a person's name, a parent company or an escrow firm instead of the customer. Example: Jane Smith pays the invoice of Acme Ltd and nobody can link it.
frequency_reason: Repeats for customers who pay as a person (L1#20); EU name checks flag mismatches (L8#25).
severity_reason: Mostly matching by eye; occasionally a returned (L3#34) or held (L8#25) payment.
unsolved_reason: ERPNext added payer-name fields (L7#4); Xero's 17-vote idea is open.
solvable_reason: A per-customer Global Account identifies the customer whatever name the bank shows; payer fields vary by bank (L5#1).
build_call_reason: Low intensity; solved as a by-product of the per-customer account built for A26.
workaround_today: Match visually; bank rules per payer name.

name: Remittance detail arrives separately and is retyped
plain: The list of which invoices a payment covers comes by separate email, PDF or portal, often late, and someone types it in. Example: a 300-row PDF must be turned into a spreadsheet before matching.
frequency_reason: Daily work on cash-application desks (L6#11, L6#12); 88% re-keyed in a 2012 survey (L5#37).
severity_reason: Hours of re-keying; missing data was the top pain at 43% (L5#37).
unsolved_reason: RemitClear, Remittance Go and Kolleno already sell into it (L2#1).
solvable_reason: AI can read PDFs and emails, but Airwallex adds only one reference string (L5#0), so the cause stays.
build_call_reason: Real but mostly a G5/G6 desk pain in a crowding market; an input to the matcher, not the first build.
workaround_today: Convert PDFs to CSV with Tabula (L7#31); search shared mailboxes and portals; attach PDFs line by line.

name: Fake bank-detail emails divert the seller's money
plain: Fraudsters email a seller's customers with 'new bank details', and payments go to the fraudster. Example: a New Zealand firm lost $11,000 when its invoices were altered.
frequency_reason: Seller-side cases are old or one-off (L8#32 2018, L8#31 2024); UK cases fell to 5,759 in 2024 (L8#29).
unsolved_reason: Callbacks and CoP/VoP name checks mitigate; courts put loss on the payer.
solvable_reason: Signature banners and callbacks help; an agent cannot stop mailbox compromise.
build_call_reason: Severe but rare on the seller side; it explains payers' caution in A38.
workaround_today: 'Our bank details have not changed' signature banner (L8#6); callbacks.

name: Several part-payments against one invoice
plain: A customer pays one invoice in parts, and tools match on amount so they lose track of what is still owed. Example: a 12-month plan pays $100 a month against a $1,200 invoice.
frequency_reason: Monthly for instalment plans (12-month plans, L1#21).
severity_reason: Wrong postings (a 20.07 remainder paid a whole 335 invoice, L7#9); Airwallex refunds leftovers (L5#13).
unsolved_reason: 104-vote Xero idea open 14 years (L2#0); Airwallex per-customer matching is all-or-nothing (L5#13).
solvable_reason: An agent can track a running balance per invoice from Airwallex deposits and webhooks.
build_call_reason: Survives, unsolved in Xero and in Airwallex's own matching, and fits an agent tracking balances on deposits.
workaround_today: Split-payment workaround; match by hand.
code_decides: Track the running balance per invoice

name: Cannot partly match a deposit or save a half-done match
plain: Accounting tools make you match a whole deposit at once; if one detail is missing you cannot park the rest or save your progress. Example: a remittance lists 40 invoices, one is unclear, and the whole match is lost.
frequency_reason: Each multi-invoice remittance with a gap; 2026 comments about four-page remittances (L2#4).
severity_reason: Restarting 99%-complete matches (L2#4) and forced overpayments (L2#3) cost hours.
unsolved_reason: Xero still cannot save partial matches after years of votes; remittance apps cover it only partly.
solvable_reason: An agent can hold a working allocation against Airwallex deposits and post to Xero only when complete.
build_call_reason: Survives, is unsolved in Xero, and an agent holding the allocation outside Xero fixes it directly.
workaround_today: Restart the match; book an overpayment and fix it later; keep a side spreadsheet.
code_decides: Hold allocations and post only when balanced

name: Overpayments and double payments handled by hand
plain: Customers sometimes pay twice or too much, and someone must decide to refund it or keep it as credit. Example: a typo sends ten times the invoice amount.
frequency_reason: 'A lot' of customers double pay (L1#28); one firm sees 1,000 a month (L1#29), but it is a high-volume domestic biller.
severity_reason: Mostly allocation time; occasional large typo (L1#5).
unsolved_reason: Xero overpayments are weak (L1#28) and Manager shows negative AR (L1#37); users do not want auto-apply (L7#25).
solvable_reason: An agent can propose credit versus refund and make the transfer, but native credit-to-balance is only 'coming soon'.
build_call_reason: Survives at low intensity; a handling rule for the agent, not a first build.
workaround_today: Apply to future invoices; hold in a liability account; refund by hand.

name: SWIFT payment delayed or untraceable in transit
plain: A wire is sent but takes days or weeks, and nobody can say where it is. Example: the customer says 'we paid' and the seller sees nothing for a week.
frequency_reason: unknown: no source measures 'we paid' claims.
severity_reason: Week-long stuck credits (L3#35); six weeks at an intermediary (L3#13).
unsolved_reason: Asking for the MT103 is a known step (L5#8); gpi tracking is not visible to sellers (L5#35).
solvable_reason: An agent can request the MT103 and watch deposit webhooks, but deposits carry no UETR (L5#9); local rails avoid SWIFT.
build_call_reason: The agent can draft the MT103 request and watch webhooks, but how often it happens is unmeasured.
workaround_today: Ask the payer for the MT103; wait three days then contact support.

name: Reserves and settlement holds make received cash unusable
plain: Card, wallet or risk reserves keep received money locked for days or months. Example: $7,600 held for 'credit risk' until February 2027.
frequency_reason: unknown: reviews only.
severity_reason: $50,000 reserves (L3#9), months-long holds (L3#11).
unsolved_reason: No tool helps.
solvable_reason: Acquiring-risk decisions an agent cannot change.
build_call_reason: Card and wallet acquiring risk outside bank-transfer receiving.
workaround_today: Leave for another provider (L3#12).

name: Getting payment proof accepted for India export tax refunds
plain: Indian exporters need a bank certificate (FIRC) to claim GST refunds, but banks now issue a different document (FIRA) that some tax officers reject. Example: a refund is rejected for a missing FIRC the bank no longer issues.
frequency_reason: At every refund claim; recurring 2025-2026 threads.
severity_reason: Refunds rejected (L4#41) and court cases (L4#44).
unsolved_reason: Many officers accept FIRA (L4#43) and courts overturn rejections.
solvable_reason: Airwallex cannot issue Indian bank documents; the RDA route still needs a manual FIRA email per transaction (L4#35).
build_call_reason: Real money for G1 but R2R can only assemble the evidence pack.
workaround_today: Withdraw in USD to get a FIRA (L4#36); argue Rule 89(2)(c).

name: Customer's accounts team recalculates the invoice and pays less
plain: The customer's system re-computes tax or converts currency its own way and pays a different figure by design. Example: a USD invoice with UK VAT is paid slightly short every month.
frequency_reason: Recurs monthly for the affected customer (L1#17 since 2024; L8#11 every month), but only two sources.
severity_reason: About $1,000 a month misbooked as bank fees (L8#11).
unsolved_reason: No tool detects it; the fix is invoice design agreed per customer.
solvable_reason: An agent can spot a repeating non-fee gap and suggest invoicing or receiving in the payer's currency; it cannot change the payer's system.
build_call_reason: Rare in the evidence; matters mainly as a reason never to label every gap a bank fee.
workaround_today: Notify the payer of the underpayment; book it as bank fees.
ai_reads: Repeating gap pattern and invoice layout
code_decides: Flag the gap as not a bank fee
person_approves: Changing invoice format with the customer

name: Some local accounts cannot take payments from foreign banks
plain: Several local receiving accounts only accept payments from banks in that country. Example: an Australian dollar account cannot be paid by a SWIFT wire from the US.
frequency_reason: unknown: a documented constraint, not user reports.
severity_reason: The payer cannot pay at all (L5#18); Singapore-onboarded Indian exporters get local rails only for SGD (L5#17).
unsolved_reason: No workaround except a SWIFT-capable account.
solvable_reason: An agent can check the payer's bank country against Airwallex coverage before proposing an account.
build_call_reason: A design constraint to code into the per-customer-account fix, not a user pain to build for.

name: Platform rupee payouts leave no bank to file the export form
plain: Since October 2026, Indian exporters must file an export form with their bank, but money paid via Wise, Skydo or Deel arrives as an ordinary rupee transfer, so no bank owns the paperwork. Example: the freelancer's bank says it sees no foreign payment to close.
frequency_reason: Every platform payout since 1 October 2026 (L4#1, L4#5).
severity_reason: Compliance uncertainty and NOC fees (L4#37); RBI may exempt personal contracts (L4#46).
unsolved_reason: Even Skydo's EDF tool leaves submission to the seller.
solvable_reason: Airwallex has no INR account; the fix sits with Indian banks and platforms.
build_call_reason: Real for G1, but Airwallex cannot supply the Indian bank side and the rules are three weeks old.
workaround_today: Ask platforms for a NOC; withdraw in USD to get a FIRA.

name: Repeat deductions from one upstream mistake
plain: One mistake upstream, like wrong terms on a purchase order or a promotion with the wrong date, causes the same short payment on many invoices. Example: every invoice is paid late because the customer's PO says net 90.
frequency_reason: unknown for small sellers; large-firm training content only.
severity_reason: The same dispute repeats across many invoices and the AP clerk cannot approve repayment (L6#7, L6#9).
unsolved_reason: No small-seller tool clusters repeat gaps; large-firm deduction tools do.
solvable_reason: An agent can cluster repeat gaps, but the fix (PO terms, who authorises repayment) is commercial.
build_call_reason: Large-firm trade-deduction pattern that small cross-border sellers seldom meet.
workaround_today: Reject wrong POs up front; find the buyer who authorised the deduction.
code_decides: Cluster repeats by customer and reason
person_approves: Raising it with the customer's buyer

name: Reminders go to customers who already paid
plain: When a payment is not matched, the system keeps chasing a customer who has paid. Example: an unallocated overpayment triggers an automatic 'you owe us' email.
frequency_reason: unknown: one Xero comment, a vendor blog and a 2022 trainer.
severity_reason: Plausible relationship harm and blocked order releases (L6#2), but no source shows lost customers.
unsolved_reason: Accounting tools send reminders on unmatched invoices regardless.
solvable_reason: An agent can pause reminders while an Airwallex deposit from that customer is unmatched.
build_call_reason: A cheap side-effect of good matching, but there is no evidence of real damage.
workaround_today: Check the bank before chasing.

name: AI auto-reconcile matches wrongly and creates duplicates
plain: Xero's new AI matching sometimes books payments to the wrong invoice and leaves duplicates for accountants to undo. Example: a client switches it on and hours of entries must be reversed.
frequency_reason: Consistent 2025-2026 comments (votes 54, 36, 21).
severity_reason: Hours of cleanup and reversed Stripe work (L2#11, L2#12).
unsolved_reason: Xero may tune it; accountants ask to limit it to bank rules (L2#9).
solvable_reason: R2R can propose matches with evidence instead of posting.
build_call_reason: Shapes R2R's design (propose, show evidence, never post blind) rather than being a separate build.
workaround_today: Turn it off; restrict to bank rules; reverse its entries.
code_decides: Score and explain each proposed match

name: Rejected or lost deposits not returned for months
plain: Money is rejected or goes missing at the provider and is neither credited nor sent back. Example: a $99,000 transfer is 'lost'.
frequency_reason: rare: Trustpilot anecdotes.
unsolved_reason: Nothing recovers it but support.
solvable_reason: A provider operations failure.
build_call_reason: Provider operations failure an agent cannot fix.
workaround_today: Chase support for months.

name: Airwallex's own matching marks short-paid payments as paid
plain: By default Airwallex marks a bank-transfer payment successful even if less arrived. Example: a $1,000 payment shows 'paid' when $980 came in.
frequency_reason: unknown: no user complaint.
severity_reason: An invoice reads 'paid' while money is missing (L5#14).
unsolved_reason: A documented default with no tool checking it.
solvable_reason: An agent can compare deposit and payment amounts via the API.
build_call_reason: A real gap R2R can fill cheaply, but no user has complained yet.

name: No agreed rule for booking a short payment
plain: When less money arrives than invoiced, accountants disagree on recording the gap as a bank fee, a currency loss or a discount. Example: a $20 gap is booked three different ways in one thread.
frequency_reason: 'Does come up often' (L1#33), but each client's accountant sets the rule once.
severity_reason: Small amounts; the only risk is editing invoices and breaking GST or audit trail (L6#30).
unsolved_reason: ERPNext documents a Deductions recipe (L7#17) and Xero, QBO, FreeAgent have fee-line workarounds.
solvable_reason: An agent can apply a saved per-client rule and log it, but it is accounting logic, not an Airwallex feature.
build_call_reason: A design setting (per-client rule plus audit log), not a pain anyone pays to remove.
workaround_today: Negative bank-charge line on the receipt; separate accounts for charges and FX.
code_decides: Apply the client's saved booking rule
person_approves: Setting the rule once per client

name: Deliberate deductions, early-pay discounts and withheld tax
plain: Some customers pay less on purpose: an early-payment discount, a disputed item or tax withheld at source. Example: a German client takes 2% off for paying early, or an Indian client deducts TDS.
frequency_reason: 418-vote discount idea (L2#18) and Skonto issue (L7#36) show small firms meet it; no rate given.
severity_reason: Under 5% of receivables but up to 30% of credit time (L6#4); valid about half the time (L6#5).
unsolved_reason: Served by HighRadius-style tools and credit-note workarounds in Xero and Invoice Ninja (L7#36).
solvable_reason: An agent can classify the gap, but the remedy is commercial; Airwallex adds nothing.
build_call_reason: Survives as a cause the classifier must recognise, but it is mostly domestic, served by others and not an Airwallex fix.
workaround_today: Create a credit note for the discount and apply it; leave deductions open or write them off.
code_decides: Classify as discount, dispute, tax or fee

name: Unidentified cash and old credits age for years
plain: Money nobody can identify, or credits nobody uses, sit in a holding account for months or years. Example: a council found unmatched cash from 2011 still in suspense.
frequency_reason: unknown for small sellers; evidence is from public bodies and large US firms.
severity_reason: Can become unclaimed-property liability inflated by audit extrapolation (L6#0, L6#1).
unsolved_reason: Large firms auto-match about 70% with software (L5#38); small sellers usually know who paid.
solvable_reason: An agent can age and chase items, but escheat rules are jurisdictional.
build_call_reason: Large-firm and public-body problem; a small cross-border seller usually knows who paid.
workaround_today: Park in suspense or Other Income; wait about 18 months or escheat.

name: Platform payouts arrive net of fees and bundled
plain: Stripe, Shopify, Amazon and similar pay out one lump net of fees covering many sales. Example: one Stripe deposit equals 137 transactions.
frequency_reason: Every payout (137 transactions per payout, L7#40).
severity_reason: Thousands of manual matches (L2#29); 20-30 minutes per payout (L7#40).
unsolved_reason: A2X, Synder and Xero's Stripe app serve the main platforms (L2#36).
solvable_reason: Payouts do not arrive with per-invoice detail on Airwallex (L5#23).
build_call_reason: Boundary segment already served by A2X-type tools; Airwallex adds nothing.
workaround_today: A2X or Synder clearing-account pattern; negative fee lines.

name: Provider closes the account and strands saved bank details
plain: The receiving provider shuts the account, payments bounce, and every customer must update saved bank details. Example: a UK telecom's customers had to switch to new details overnight.
frequency_reason: rare: one detailed case plus termination reviews.
severity_reason: All receipts bounce and capital frozen (L3#17, L3#19).
unsolved_reason: Ombudsman lets providers close without reason (L3#33).
solvable_reason: A provider decision an agent cannot override; concentrating customers on provider accounts raises the exit cost.
build_call_reason: Rare but severe; a risk to disclose for the per-customer-account fix.
workaround_today: Publish new details on invoices and portal (L3#19).

name: Poor rupee rates and new fees on receiving apps
plain: Indian receiving apps give rates below the bank's and add fees. Example: about INR 10,000 less on a 1.9 lakh payment.
frequency_reason: Every receipt on that platform.
severity_reason: About 5% gap (L3#37); 1% new fee (L3#38).
unsolved_reason: Sellers switch providers or run two rails.
solvable_reason: Airwallex FX quotes could compare, but there is no INR account.
build_call_reason: A pricing complaint solved by switching, not reconciliation.
workaround_today: Switch provider.

name: One payment covering many invoices
plain: A customer pays several invoices in one transfer and the seller has to split it. Example: one $5,000 transfer covers 20 invoices.
frequency_reason: Common for some clients (about 20 invoices per payment, L2#21).
severity_reason: Tedious rather than costly.
unsolved_reason: FreeAgent splits across 100 invoices (L2#32); QBO Undeposited Funds (L1#14); Xero batch deposits.
solvable_reason: An agent can split it, but tools already do.
build_call_reason: Solved by hand in mainstream tools; only the rare 50-plus-invoice edge remains.
workaround_today: Undeposited Funds plus a combined deposit; FreeAgent split; Xero batch deposit.

name: Refunding an overpayment abroad costs fees and time
plain: Sending extra money back abroad costs a fee and can take weeks. Example: a $50 refund loses $2 to fees.
frequency_reason: unknown: no small seller describes it.
severity_reason: About 2.00 fee per refund (L5#15); refunds issued late (L6#28).
unsolved_reason: Airwallex's credit-to-balance option is only 'coming soon' (L5#15).
solvable_reason: An agent can choose credit versus refund and send the transfer.
build_call_reason: Evidence is docs and public-body policies only.
workaround_today: Hold overpayments before refunding to the original payer (L6#29).

name: Bank statement imports break or create duplicates
plain: Importing bank files into some tools drops descriptions or duplicates rows. Example: two identical $100 payments are merged into one and the balance is wrong.
frequency_reason: unknown: open-source tool issues.
severity_reason: Wrong balances when identical payments collapse (L7#22).
unsolved_reason: Most were fixed within 1-4 days (L7#18, L7#19).
solvable_reason: An agent on the Airwallex API avoids file parsing.
build_call_reason: Hobby and open-source tool defects; the useful rule goes into the matcher.
workaround_today: Wait for the maintainer's fix; hand-create fee rows.

name: Customers distrust an account in another country
plain: Some customers hesitate to pay a bank in a different country from the seller. Example: a UK firm's Danish IBAN stalls with large customers.
frequency_reason: No 2024-2026 source; one 2018 thread.
severity_reason: Large customers stalled for days or months (L8#14).
unsolved_reason: EU law bars IBAN discrimination.
solvable_reason: An agent can offer an account in the payer's own country.
build_call_reason: Old, thin evidence.
workaround_today: Use a local-country account.
code_decides: Choose an account in that country

name: Banks unprepared and inconsistent on export forms
plain: Bank branches and relationship managers do not yet know the new export-form process, and each bank does it differently. Example: one bank replies by email in hours, another ignores a request for a month.
frequency_reason: Many early-October 2026 reports.
severity_reason: Delays from days to a month (L4#27).
unsolved_reason: Bank SOPs are still settling (L4#12 shows it can be easy).
solvable_reason: A bank process R2R cannot change.
build_call_reason: Launch teething at Indian banks; likely to fade.
workaround_today: Escalate to the trade branch; email the bank.

name: Bank fees and demands for each export form
plain: Banks charge per export form and ask for current accounts or extra registrations. Example: a fee for every form filed.
frequency_reason: Per form filed (L4#3).
severity_reason: Rs 1,000-2,000 anecdotes; Regulation 19(3) limits charges (L4#45).
unsolved_reason: Bank pricing with no tool involved.
solvable_reason: A bank price an agent cannot remove.
build_call_reason: Bank pricing outside R2R's control.
workaround_today: Pay the fee or switch banks.

name: Bank holds incoming money until export form or IEC is given
plain: Some Indian banks will not credit a foreign payment until the export form or an exporter code is filed. Example: a consultant's USD payment is stuck because the system will not let it proceed.
frequency_reason: unknown: one first-person case; rest vendor warnings.
severity_reason: Inward USD blocked (L4#13).
unsolved_reason: Bank systems still settling.
solvable_reason: An agent can pre-fill the form from invoice data; the bank decides release.
build_call_reason: One first-person case; mostly competitor warnings.
workaround_today: File the EDF first; supply IEC.

name: Matching per-customer account transfers to open payments
plain: Giving each customer its own receiving account so payments match automatically. Example: Customer A always pays into account A.
frequency_reason: unknown.
severity_reason: Not a pain once native.
unsolved_reason: Airwallex Payments ships 'Dedicated Account per Customer' (L5#12).
solvable_reason: Native on Airwallex in nine regions (not India).
build_call_reason: Native for most of G3; R2R must build on it and cover only the gaps.
workaround_today: Use Airwallex native feature.

name: Settled deposit later reversed by the payer's bank
plain: Money already credited can be recalled by the payer's bank after it has been matched. Example: a paid invoice suddenly becomes unpaid again.
frequency_reason: No user report.
severity_reason: Silent re-opening of a paid invoice.
unsolved_reason: Thinly documented.
solvable_reason: The deposit.reversed webhook lets an agent re-open the invoice.
build_call_reason: Documented state, no user complaint.

name: Up-front deposits sit unallocated until the invoice exists
plain: A customer pays an advance before the final invoice exists, and the money sits unmatched. Example: a 30% deposit stays as an unexplained bank line for weeks.
frequency_reason: unknown: one comment.
severity_reason: Weeks unallocated (L2#20).
unsolved_reason: Xero's 2026 deposits feature covers Stripe only, not bank transfers.
solvable_reason: An agent can tag an advance to a quote or customer and apply it later.
build_call_reason: One comment; no breadth evidence.
workaround_today: Leave the bank line unreconciled until the invoice is final.
code_decides: Hold as advance for that customer
person_approves: Applying it to the final invoice

name: Upwork or Payoneer net payouts break India tax matching
plain: Marketplaces pay Indian sellers net of fees, so the bank credit never equals the invoice filed for GST or the export bill. Example: a $1,000 export bill gets a $227 payout.
frequency_reason: unknown: two items.
severity_reason: GST mismatch notice risk (L4#33); export bill cannot close (L6#18).
unsolved_reason: Fix is a CA's gross-up workpaper.
solvable_reason: Money flows through Upwork and Payoneer, not Airwallex.
build_call_reason: Money does not touch Airwallex.
workaround_today: CA gross-up workpaper; batch withdrawals.

name: SWIFT reference text cut or useless for matching
plain: The free-text note on an international wire is cut short or carries nothing useful. Example: a reference ends with '+' because the message format chopped it.
frequency_reason: unknown: bank guides from 2021-2024 and two payer-side posts.
severity_reason: Forces manual matching (L1#15).
unsolved_reason: Should ease as ISO 20022 replaces MT.
solvable_reason: Airwallex passes on only the reference it receives; local rails avoid SWIFT.
build_call_reason: Likely to fade with ISO 20022; no 2026 first-person receiver complaint.
workaround_today: Match manually by amount and date.

name: Payer differs from the invoiced party so an Indian bank holds the credit
plain: If the payer's name differs from the name on the invoice, an Indian bank may treat it as a third-party payment and hold it. Example: a designer's payment is held until she proves brand and legal names are the same.
frequency_reason: unknown: one vendor blog.
severity_reason: Credit held until proof (L3#40).
unsolved_reason: Bank KYC decides.
solvable_reason: An agent can prepare proof that both names are one entity.
build_call_reason: Vendor-only evidence.
workaround_today: Prove the names are the same entity.

name: Month-end close delayed by unmatched receipts
plain: Books cannot be closed while receipts are unmatched. Example: the close slips a week waiting for remittances.
frequency_reason: unknown: no first-person close-delay story.
severity_reason: Unmeasured delay; vendor and bank claims only (L5#34).
unsolved_reason: One user already scripts Claude to find items (L2#24).
solvable_reason: Faster matching on Airwallex deposits would help.
build_call_reason: No measured delay.
workaround_today: Script an LLM over a CSV export (L2#24).

name: Bookkeepers would pay to fix reconciliation
plain: Bookkeepers serving many clients feel reconciliation most, but it is unclear they would pay much. Example: Upwork clean-up gigs at $5 to $250.
frequency_reason: unknown.
severity_reason: Low price ceiling (L6#31).
unsolved_reason: Many tools compete.
solvable_reason: Depends on the product built.
build_call_reason: No willingness-to-pay evidence.
workaround_today: Outsource clean-ups to cheap gigs.

name: Retention held back on invoices
plain: Some trades hold back a share of each invoice until the job is done, and tools cannot track it. Example: a builder gets 95% now and 5% a year later.
frequency_reason: unknown for cross-border sellers; the 59-vote idea is construction and CIS.
severity_reason: Tracking burden; the workaround fails with CIS (L1#23).
unsolved_reason: Xero said it is not planned (L1#23).
solvable_reason: Domestic construction pain outside Airwallex receiving.
build_call_reason: Domestic construction pain outside R2R's segments.
workaround_today: Negative line to a balance-sheet account.

name: Accounting software computes currency gains wrongly
plain: Some tools post bank charges as currency gains or ignore earlier revaluations. Example: a realised gain shows INR 18,745 when it should be INR 177.
frequency_reason: unknown: ERP bug reports.
severity_reason: Large wrong figures (L7#2) and fees hidden in FX (L7#0).
unsolved_reason: Most issues were closed or fixed.
solvable_reason: Tool defects outside Airwallex.
build_call_reason: ERP defects, not a market pain.
workaround_today: Manual correcting journals.

name: No bank feeds for Indian banks in accounting tools
plain: Some tools cannot pull transactions from Indian banks at all. Example: ERPNext has no feed for HDFC or ICICI.
frequency_reason: unknown: one issue.
severity_reason: Manual statement uploads.
unsolved_reason: Still open in ERPNext (L7#12).
solvable_reason: Airwallex has no INR account to supply the Indian bank side.
build_call_reason: R2R cannot supply Indian bank data.
workaround_today: Upload statements; use Tally or Zoho.

name: Payment from or to the wrong company in a group
plain: A customer pays one company in a group for invoices from a sister company, or cannot tell which account was paid. Example: one $10,000 cheque covers $7,000 owed to a sister firm.
frequency_reason: rare: one thread and a payer-side idea.
severity_reason: Liability-account workaround (L1#36).
unsolved_reason: QBO cannot apply across companies.
solvable_reason: Separate Global Accounts per entity would make it visible.
build_call_reason: No frequency data.
workaround_today: Liability account plus a second deposit.

name: Credit notes and refunds are hard to match
plain: Credit notes and incoming refunds are awkward to match against payments. Example: a half-refunded advance still shows $1,000 open.
frequency_reason: unknown: mostly single-tool reports.
severity_reason: Confusing ageing and audit-trail clutter (L1#11, L7#14).
unsolved_reason: Xero released credit-note selection to all customers on 20 March 2026 (L2#19).
solvable_reason: Remaining cases are ERP defects, not receiving problems.
build_call_reason: Solved in Xero; what is left are ERP bugs.
workaround_today: Different journal workarounds per accountant.

name: Cash forecast assumes invoices are paid on the due date
plain: Forecasts treat every invoice as paid on its due date, ignoring habitual late payers. Example: a customer who always pays 20 days late is forecast as on time.
frequency_reason: unknown.
severity_reason: Misleading forecasts.
unsolved_reason: Xero Analytics Cash Flow Manager (2026) and Float predict from behaviour.
solvable_reason: Deposit history could feed it, but tools already do this.
build_call_reason: Overtaken by 2026 forecasting tools.
workaround_today: Use Float or Xero Analytics.

name: Tiny rounding leftovers and false currency gains
plain: Software rounding leaves a few cents open on invoices or invents a small currency gain. Example: an invoice still shows $0.02 owing after full payment.
frequency_reason: unknown: two single-user reports.
severity_reason: Cent-level amounts that replies call immaterial (L1#9).
unsolved_reason: A bulk write-off below a threshold clears it; the precision bug is Xero's to fix (L2#23).
solvable_reason: An agent can check a residual is not a real short pay, but the cause sits in accounting software.
build_call_reason: Immaterial amounts caused by accounting-software rounding.
workaround_today: Bulk write-off of balances below a threshold.
code_decides: Below threshold and not a real short pay

name: One tax document required per payment (Mexico)
plain: Mexican rules need one fiscal document per payment, but tools create one per invoice. Example: a payment for three invoices produces three records.
frequency_reason: One 2019 issue.
severity_reason: Compliance mismatch.
unsolved_reason: Open Odoo issue.
solvable_reason: Outside R2R's markets.
build_call_reason: Country-specific and outside R2R's markets.

name: Customer's payment network keeps a fee from each payment
plain: Some US customers pay through networks like Paymode-X that keep a fee, so the seller looks short-paid. Example: a $2,000 invoice arrives as $1,990.
frequency_reason: unknown breadth: every payment from that payer, but one thread.
severity_reason: Small fees.
unsolved_reason: Fee-line bank rules handle it.
solvable_reason: US domestic AP network, unrelated to Airwallex receiving.
build_call_reason: US domestic pattern from one thread, outside cross-border receiving.
workaround_today: Record the fee as a negative line instead of editing invoices.

name: Returned wire comes back minus a fee
plain: When a wire bounces, a bank keeps a fee, so less comes back than was sent. Example: a $500 wire to a wrong account returns as $480.
frequency_reason: One thread.
severity_reason: Small fee and a known answer.
unsolved_reason: Book the return and the fee separately (L1#6).
solvable_reason: Deposit webhooks show rejected or reversed money, but the fee is a bank charge.
build_call_reason: Rare, low value and solved by a known entry.
workaround_today: Book the return and the fee as two entries.
code_decides: Split into return and fee entries
